correct_findings: The analysis examined 21 normalized Linux Auditd PROCTITLE records selected from an original dataset containing 108 records
Six selected records contain sudo chmod u+s vuln, which requests setting the SUID permission bit
Six selected records contain sudo setcap cap_setuid+ep ./priv_esc, which requests assigning CAP_SETUID capabilities
Nine additional records provide administrative context involving auditd and SplunkForwarder services
The evidence supports identifying potentially privilege-sensitive commands requiring investigation
The source timestamps were correctly derived from the original Auditd epoch values
The available evidence does not establish successful privilege escalation.
incorrect_findings: Mistral characterized the activity as apparently benign without sufficient authorization evidence
The model attributed the commands to system administrators although the source records contain no verified user identity
Multiple Auditd PROCTITLE records were interpreted as repeated command attempts without establishing independent executions
The potential attack indicator lacked explicit evidence references
The incident timeline included an abbreviated placeholder row without a valid evidence reference
The IOC extraction component incorrectly classified auditd.service and SplunkForwarder.service as domains and auditd as a hostname.
missing_evidence: Associated SYSCALL and EXECVE records confirming execution outcomes
USER_AUTH and authentication records establishing user identity and sudo authorization
Original UID, EUID, and audit user identifiers
File metadata confirming whether SUID permissions were successfully changed
File capability verification confirming whether CAP_SETUID was assigned
Evidence of subsequent execution of vuln or priv_esc
Evidence of successful UID changes or root access
Change approval records and administrative context
Complete evidence references for all selected Auditd records.
hallucinations: Unsupported attribution of the observed commands to system administrators
Unsupported benign characterization without independent authorization evidence
Unsupported interpretation of repeated PROCTITLE records as independently confirmed command attempts
Incorrect IOC classification of Linux service names as network domains and the auditd source label as a hostname
No confirmed fabricated source events or timestamp mismatches were identified in the displayed analysis.
review.notes: LT-02 Human Analyst Review. Analysis AN-20261018-221905-552c examined 21 normalized Linux Auditd PROCTITLE records selected from 108 original records. Source integrity, command decoding, evidence mapping, timestamp conversion, and parser compatibility were previously verified. Mistral identified two privilege-sensitive command patterns involving SUID permission modification and CAP_SETUID capability assignment. Automated validation generated two medium-severity flags concerning missing evidence references and an incomplete timeline row. Both findings require documentation correction. Additional manual review identified unsupported benign classification, unverified administrator attribution, unsupported assumptions about repeated independent executions, and incorrect IOC categorization. The available evidence does not establish successful command execution, unauthorized access, or completed privilege escalation. Original evidence, normalized records, evidence mappings, and AI output must remain unchanged. Human Review Status: Corrected.
